newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: TENNIS-MARTINEZ CRASHES OUT OF EUROPEAN INDOORS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-MARTINEZ CRASHES OUT OF EUROPEAN INDOORS.

text.p: Spanish top seed Conchita Martinez crashed out of the European indoor championship on Wednesday, losing 6-4 6-4 to Belgium's Sabine Appelmans.
Appelmans, ranked 23rd in the world, secured the only service break in the opening set in the ninth game and kept up the pressure in the second to take a commanding 4-0 lead.
At 5-1, Martinez, the world number three, finally won three consecutive games but an unlikely comeback was ruled out when Appelmans held serve to clinch the match.
"I had a lot of chances in the first set when she was serving and didn't take them," said Martinez. "It's just a bad day. The loss doesn't bother me. I'm still number three in the world.
"It's the end of the year and I'm very tired physically and mentally."
Fourth seed Jana Novotna and Swiss teenager Martina Hingis, seeded fifth, both posted second round wins to move into the quarter-finals.
Hingis, fresh from her first career tournament win last week in Filderstadt, needed just 57 minutes to dispose of Irina Spirlea 6-3 6-3.

In her opening match on Tuesday the 16-year-old Swiss also spent less than an hour on court, dispatching Japan's Naoka Sawamatsu in 49 minutes. "I feel good and I'm ready to take on anybody," said the world number nine afterwards.
